title: Low-confidence merge probe — annotator heuristics and sampling notes
content:
Purpose and quick summary:

This is my scratchpad for rules and probing experiments around when to automatically merge low-confidence labels vs. send for adjudication. We have increasing volume of partial/low-agreement labels where reviewers want an automated first pass to collapse obviously-duplicative spans without losing subtle cases. Goal: reduce human adjudication queue by ~30% while keeping precision loss <2% on reviewed benchmark.

Definitions (working):
- low-confidence candidate: model or annotator confidence < 0.55 (float) or annotator agreement score < 0.6 on multi-pass sampling.
- mergeable pair: two spans that refer to the same entity mention (same normalized text or trivial variants) and whose combined label set does not change the downstream resolution (eg both PERSON -> PERSON).

High-level rule sketch (do not push to prod yet):
1) Fast-merge if: normalized_text_equal == True AND label_type_equal == True AND token-overlap > 0.85 AND both confidences < 0.6 but distance-from-boundary small (trim punctuation) -> auto-merge.
2) Candidate-merge with sample audit if: normalized_text_close (levenshtein <=2 for <=8 chars OR fuzzy-match ratio > 0.9) AND label_type_equal AND annotator-disagreement <= 0.25 -> put into "probation" batch (auto-merge but sample 5% for human QA).
3) Defer-to-adjudication if: label_type_conflict (PERSON vs ORG) OR semantic-role-mismatch (e.g., location vs product) OR token-overlap between .4 and .85 AND any annotate says "compound/uncertain" OR multi-token hyphenation / slashed forms present.
4) Special-case: numeric ranges, currency, and date spans -> conservative: require adjudication if either span contains numeric separators or multiple tokens representing normalized values (example: "Q1 2023" vs "2023 Q1").

Sampling plan for trials (2-week pilot):
- Random sample of 12k low-confidence pairs from last 30 days (balanced across source domains: tickets, chats, docs).
- Split into three arms: aggressive-merge (rules 1+2), conservative (only rule 1), baseline (no auto-merge).
- Audit: 1.5k human-reviewed items per arm (labeling team) + MCQ-style checks for merge correctness.
- Metrics: human adjudication reduction (%), precision of merges (human vs auto), recall change on downstream entity linking, estimated token cost saved in adjudication time.

Edge examples noted while prototyping:
- "A. Smith" vs "A Smith" — punctuation trimmed usually safe to merge when matching initials/last-name but be careful with institutional names like "A. Smith Labs". Add rule: don't merge if adjacent token indicates organization (Ltd/Inc/Labs).
- Phone numbers with formatting differences: +1 (415) 555-0102 vs 415-555-0102 -> normalize heavily, prefer automated merge but mark for sampling if country codes present.
- Hyphenation flips: "state-of-the-art" vs "state of the art" -> often same; merge if stopword normalization triggers and POS sketches match.
- Abbreviations+expansions: "Intl." vs "International" for org types -> merge if suffix token after expansion matches known suffix list. Keep a small suffix whitelist file.

Heuristic scoring (temporary):
- normalized_text_match = 1.0 if exact after unicode normalization and casefold; else fuzzy_score in [0,1].
- token_overlap = intersection/union of token sets (after punctuation and stopword trim).
- label_alignment = 1 if majority label match; else 0.
- automated_merge_score = 0.6*normalized_text_match + 0.25*token_overlap + 0.15*(1 - annotator_disagreement)
- threshold for auto-merge: >= 0.85 for fast-merge; >= 0.72 for probationary auto-merge (with sample audit).

Logging / instrumentation needs:
- Tag each auto-merge with rule-id and features used so we can slice errors later.
- Store pre-merge and post-merge canonical forms for quick diffs in dashboard.
- Add a "why-blocked" field to explain deferrals returned to adjudicators (helps faster triage).

Open questions / TODOs (short):
- What's the right sampling fraction for probation batches to maintain 95% CI +/- 2% on merge precision? (ask stats team)
- Should we incorporate downstream embedding similarity (entity embedding cosine > 0.88) as a signal for ambiguous text matches? Risk: cross-domain variance. Run small test.
- Integrate with existing adjudication UI (current flow expects per-item, need to send merged pairs view). POC ticket: UI-789.
- Build a tiny suffix/affix lookup (company suffixes, cert abbreviations) for safe vs risky merges. Start list: Inc, Ltd, LLC, GmbH, Co, Labs, Institute, University -> store as plain CSV.

Quick notes from last sync with labeling team (2025-02-07):
- Marco: prefer visible diffs in adjudication UI rather than full context removal.
- Jin: wants a "revert auto-merge" quick button (we can capture as a patch and count reverts as error metric).
- Ops: watch for throughput spike when sampling size increases; prefer rolling window sampling.

Example items (handy for unit tests):
1) Input corpus: "Acme Inc." vs "Acme Incorporated" -> expect auto-merge probation (suffix match + fuzzy close).
2) "W. E. B. Du Bois" vs "W.E.B DuBois" -> require strong normalization, merge if punctuation-normalized forms equal.
3) "2021-01-02" vs "01/02/2021" -> treat as dates; do not auto-merge unless date-normalizer agrees.
4) "Washington (state)" vs "Washington" -> ambiguous (state vs person vs org) -> adjudicate.

Mini action list (me):
- [ ] Wire up sampling query to annotation DB (SQL stub in /scripts/sample_low_conf.tsv).
- [ ] Build offline scorer script to compute automated_merge_score and export top/bottom deciles for review.
- [ ] Draft PR for lightweight suffix list and add to shared-config repo. Link: PR-324 (WIP).
- [ ] Create test cases above and add to unit-tests for merge heuristics repo.

Notes-to-self (voicey):
- Keep pilot small and measurable. People panic when automation hits weird stuff (rightly).
- Document false-positive examples asap so triage can add quick filters.
- The goal is not to be clever; it's to reduce repetitive adjudication and free up human judgment for real hard conflicts.

If this grows beyond small pilot: consider a simple ML classifier (random forest or small transformer) trained on features above + embedding similarity to predict merge-safe. But only after we get reliable labeled pilot data (target n ~10k).

End of scratchpad entry (will iterate).
